title: Get started with zumir
text: rfunction() takes numeric R function compiles native code. result arguments returns exactly R function returns. accepts doubles, loops indices, conditions usual maths; anything else refused construct named.
code: csum_r <- function(x) {   y <- numeric(length(x))   acc <- 0   for (i in seq_along(x)) {     acc <- acc + x[i]     y[i] <- acc   }   y } csum <- rfunction(csum_r)  x <- c(1, 2, NA, 4) csum(x) identical(csum(x), csum_r(x))

title: Get started with zumir
text: cfunction() takes source one C function returns R function calls . Arguments named allocated returned. Lengths come int argument name.
code: # Open: should one source hold several functions, returned as a list? (Q2) sq <- cfunction("   void sq(int n, const double *x, double *y) {     for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) y[i] = x[i] * x[i];   }", out = "y", n = "n")  sq(x = c(1, 2, 3))

title: Get started with zumir
text: function returns int double gives value back directly. Arguments can int, double, const int *, const double *, int * double *. source may use C maths library memory string functions, can’t include system headers call R’s API.
code: dot <- cfunction("   double dot(int n, const double *x, const double *y) {     double s = 0;     for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += x[i] * y[i];     return s;   }", n = "n")  dot(x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c(4, 5, 6))

title: What zumir has, and what runs here — zumir_info
text: load, zumir compiles calls small function natively MIR's interpreter. tier reported four capabilities, fail separately: compile (MIR builds function tier), entry (address C can call), run (calling gives right answer) external (can call C library function, exp). tier available four hold. tiers need memory writable executable, interpreter , since MIR generates small call bridges . system refuses memory (SELinux deny_execmem, seccomp policies hardened containers), neither tier runs, zumir_tier() "none". reason column says refused. macOS, R needs com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit entitlement CRAN's build carries.
